# Fixtures that must never be auto-run by a pull request's scoped conformance.
#
# ci.yml scopes a PR's conformance to the fixtures the PR touched. Some fixtures
# cannot pass in CI no matter what the PR changed - the blocker is the test
# environment or the job's time budget, not the diff - so running them turns
# every PR that touches them red and bills Azure for the privilege. They are
# listed here and subtracted from the PR scope, with the reason on each.
#
# Same format as conformance-matrix.txt: one fixture per line, '#' comments and
# blank lines ignored. A name may NOT appear in both files - conformance-scope.sh
# fails the run if one does, so the two cannot drift into disagreement.
#
# This file does NOT affect push-to-main or nightly. Those are driven purely by
# conformance-matrix.txt; a fixture absent from that file already does not run.
#
# Removing a line here is how a fixture becomes PR-eligible again - do it once
# the blocker below is gone.

# --- Blocked by the CI environment: no diff can make these pass -------------

# Needs a real owned domain (Azure serves an ownership challenge the CI
# subscription cannot answer).
custom-hostname-binding

# Azure validates an App Service certificate against a verified custom domain on
# the referenced plan; with no verified domain, no certificate is accepted.
app-service-certificate

# The conformance subscription has a dedicated-VM quota of 0, and an App Service
# plan of ANY sku runs on dedicated VMs - verified 2026-08-28 against both B1
# (Basic) and F1 (Free); both are refused identically:
#
#   Code: Unauthorized
#   Operation cannot be completed without additional quota.
#   Current Limit (Total VMs): 0 / Amount required for this deployment: 1
#
# So no plan can be created there, and every Microsoft.Web fixture that needs one
# fails on the plan rather than on anything the plugin did. Raising the
# subscription's "Total Regional vCPUs"/App Service quota is the only unblock;
# remove these four lines when that lands. AZURE::Web::StaticSite is unaffected
# (Static Web Apps are serverless) and stays in PR scope.
#
# CRUD for all four is covered by the mocked integration tests; run live against
# a quota-bearing subscription with:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=app-service-plan
app-service-plan
web-app
function-app
web-app-slot

# virtual-hub passes locally end to end (68m50s) but cannot pass in CI. ARM
# refuses DeleteVirtualHub while routingState is still Provisioning, which runs
# ~11 min past the create LRO reporting Succeeded, so the CRUD phase measures
# ~59 min - longer than the OIDC client assertion stays valid. The run dies in the
# final phase with:
#
#   AADSTS700024: Client assertion is not within its valid time range
#
# The plugin waits for the router correctly (see VirtualHub.Delete); this is a
# credential-lifetime limit, not a plugin bug. Remove this line once CI can
# refresh auth mid-phase. Run locally with:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=virtual-hub TIMEOUT=90
virtual-hub

# --- Exceed the conformance-tests job's timeout-minutes: 120 ----------------
# Measured lifecycles: vpn-gateway ~60 min, the two virtual-network-gateway
# fixtures ~60-90 min, and a lifecycle runs create + update + destroy +
# recreate + OOB-delete. scripts/ci/run-conformance-phase.sh already carries
# their per-command budgets, so raising the job cap is the only change needed to
# make them runnable.
vpn-gateway
virtual-network-gateway
virtual-network-gateway-connection

# --- Wave 2 -----------------------------------------------------------------

# Management group operations are tenant-scoped, and no principal on the test
# subscription has any role assignment above subscription scope - verified with
#   az role assignment list --scope /subscriptions/<sub> --include-inherited
# which returns only subscription-scoped Owner/Contributor/Reader rows, and with
#   az account management-group list
#   -> AuthorizationFailed: ... does not have authorization to perform action
#      'Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/read' over scope
#      '/providers/Microsoft.Management'
# The handlers are implemented and unit-tested; they cannot be exercised live
# until a principal is granted a role at the tenant root. Remove these two lines
# when that lands. Run locally against a tenant-root-capable login with:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=management-group
management-group
management-group-subscription-association

# A Managed HSM bills at roughly $3.20/hour from the moment it is created - by
# far the most expensive resource in the suite - and takes 20-30 min to
# provision. It also has soft-delete permanently on with a 7-day minimum
# retention, so the conformance lifecycle's OOB-delete-then-recreate would hit
# "name already in a soft-deleted state" unless the purge succeeds first. A run
# that is killed mid-lifecycle therefore leaks a resource costing ~$2,300/month
# until someone notices. Not worth running on every PR that touches the fixture.
# The handler is implemented and unit-tested. Run it deliberately, and check
# afterwards that nothing is left in `az keyvault list-deleted --resource-type mhsm`:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=managed-hsm TIMEOUT=120
managed-hsm

# --- Wave 3 -----------------------------------------------------------------

# A Log Analytics dedicated cluster carries a minimum capacity reservation that
# bills whether or not it is used, and `armoperationalinsights` v1.2.0 speaks
# api-version 2021-06-01, whose Capacity enum floor is 500 GB/day
# (CapacityFiveHundred). Microsoft's later 100 GB/day floor is not reachable
# through this SDK version, so there is no cheap variant to fall back to.
# Provisioning is also measured in hours - a workspace cannot be linked until the
# cluster finishes - against the ~45 min ceiling at which CI's OIDC client
# assertion expires and the run dies with AADSTS700024. The create LRO simply
# stays InProgress for the whole wait. Handler and schema are implemented and
# unit-tested. Run deliberately, against a subscription where the reservation is
# acceptable:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=log-analytics-cluster TIMEOUT=240
log-analytics-cluster

# `armoperationalinsights` v1.2.0's TablesClient exposes only Get, Update (PATCH)
# and NewListByWorkspacePager - there is no PUT and no DELETE. A workspace table
# is created by the workspace and cannot be removed, so the resource adopts an
# existing table and owns only its retention, and Delete resets retention to the
# workspace default. (Terraform's azurerm_log_analytics_workspace_table has the
# same semantics.) That cannot satisfy the CRUD lifecycle's out-of-band delete
# phase: steps 22-24 delete the resource outside formae and then require `sync`
# to drop it from inventory, but Read on a built-in table keeps succeeding, so
# the resource never disappears. This is an SDK capability limit, not a plugin
# defect, and no diff can make the phase pass.
log-analytics-table

# PROVISIONAL - re-check once wave 3's Automation group merges.
# A workspace linked service has exactly two possible targets and neither was
# available when the fixture was written: `Cluster` needs the dedicated cluster
# skipped above, and `Automation` needs an Automation account, which this plugin
# did not implement at the time. AZURE::Automation::Account arrives in the same
# wave, so this fixture should be reworked to point at one and this line removed
# - it is a fixture-shape blocker, not an environment or SDK limit.
log-analytics-linked-service

# Both of these are blocked on a field the PARENT schema does not have, not on
# anything the handler does. Handlers and mocked integration tests are complete;
# remove each line when the parent gains what ARM demands.

# ARM refuses a local user unless the account has a hierarchical namespace, and
# SFTP additionally needs isSftpEnabled. `schema/pkl/storage/storageaccount.pkl`
# models none of isHnsEnabled / isSftpEnabled / isLocalUserEnabled, so no fixture
# can build a suitable parent and [Create] fails with ARM's own "local users are
# not supported on this account". Fix: three fields on StorageAccount.
storage-local-user

# ARM requires the blob change feed on the source account and blob versioning on
# the destination. Both live on the blob-service singleton
# (storageAccounts/blobServices/default); StorageAccount carries neither and there
# is no BlobServiceProperties resource type in the tree, so the create fails with
# ChangeFeedNotEnabled. Fix: a BlobServiceProperties type, or change-feed and
# versioning fields on StorageAccount.
storage-object-replication-policy

# Self-hosted gateways require the Developer or Premium tier. Every APIM fixture
# in this wave uses Consumption, which is the only tier CI can afford: a
# throwaway Consumption instance reached Succeeded in 159s on 2026-09-02, while
# Developer/Standard take 30-45 min and blow the ~45 min point at which the OIDC
# client assertion expires (AADSTS700024). ARM rejects the create outright on
# Consumption. Handler, schema and fixture are complete; the SKU stays as it is.
api-management-gateway

# ARM addresses a tag description by the id of an APIM tag that must already
# exist, and does not create it as a side effect. There is no way to create that
# tag from anything in scope: `TagClient` is deliberately unwired and the Api
# contract carries no APIM-tag field, so the fixture 404s at [Create]. Handler,
# schema, test and fixture are complete and work the day
# AZURE::ApiManagement::Tag exists. Remove this line then.
api-management-api-tag-description

# The Consumption tier has no user store, no group store and no subscription
# store, so these five cannot be created there. Every APIM fixture in this wave
# is Consumption because it is the only tier CI can afford - a Consumption
# instance reached Succeeded in 159s on 2026-09-02, against 30-45 min for a
# dedicated tier and a ~45 min ceiling where the OIDC assertion expires
# (AADSTS700024). Handlers, schemas, tests and fixtures are complete for all
# five; only the tier blocks them.
#
# Evidence, from Microsoft's own tier matrix
# (learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/api-management-features):
#   "Developer portal2 | (Consumption) NO | ..."
#   "2 Including related functionality such as users, groups, issues,
#    applications, and email templates and notifications."
# and from the service limits page, Consumption column:
#   "Subscriptions | N/A"      "Users | N/A"
#
# ProductGroup is blocked transitively: its fixture names the built-in
# `developers` group, which does not exist on Consumption, and a custom group
# would not help because the group store itself is absent.
#
# Remove these five lines if the conformance subscription ever gets a dedicated
# tier that CI can wait for.
api-management-group
api-management-group-user
api-management-user
api-management-subscription
api-management-product-group

# Both of these are singleton / verb-shaped resources whose Read keeps succeeding
# after an out-of-band delete, so the CRUD lifecycle's OOB-delete phase can never
# observe them disappear. Same structural reason as log-analytics-table above, and
# confirmed live on 2026-09-03:
#
#   [OOB Del] Resource should be removed from inventory after OOB delete + sync:
#             timeout waiting for resource ...
#
# storage-queue-service-properties is the per-account queue-service singleton named
# `default`: there is no create and no delete, only SetServiceProperties, and
# "delete" means resetting it to empty - after which Read still returns the
# singleton. storage-blob-container-immutability-policy is verb-shaped in the same
# way (CreateOrUpdateImmutabilityPolicy / DeleteImmutabilityPolicy with an If-Match
# ETag) and its state is read off the parent container, which survives.
#
# Handlers, schemas and mocked integration tests are complete for both, and every
# phase before OOB-delete passes. This is a shape mismatch between a singleton and
# a lifecycle that assumes create/destroy symmetry, not a plugin defect - so there
# is nothing a diff can fix.
storage-queue-service-properties
storage-blob-container-immutability-policy

# Azure permits only ONE Network Manager per overlapping scope, and on this
# subscription the only available scope IS the subscription. Confirmed live on
# 2026-09-03:
#
#   RESPONSE 400: BadRequest
#   "Cannot have two Network Managers applied to the same object overlapping
#    scope accesses. Scope id: /subscriptions/<sub>"
#
# Every Network Manager fixture declares a manager scoped to the subscription, and
# the CRUD lifecycle additionally creates an out-of-band manager at the same scope
# for its discovery and OOB phases. So these fixtures conflict with each other AND
# with their own out-of-band manager - the second create at that scope always
# fails, whatever the plugin does.
#
# Management group scope is what would separate them, and it is unavailable here:
# no principal on this subscription holds a role above subscription scope
# (`az account management-group list` returns AuthorizationFailed), which is why
# group 10 was scoped to subscriptions only in the first place. The constraint that
# made the group buildable is the same one that makes it untestable in parallel.
#
# Handlers, schemas and mocked integration tests are complete for all eight types,
# and `network-manager-static-member` additionally reached [Update] before failing,
# so the code paths do work against ARM. Remove these lines if the subscription
# ever gains management-group scope, or if the harness learns to serialise fixtures
# that declare an exclusive scope.
network-manager
network-manager-network-group
network-manager-static-member
network-manager-subscription-connection
network-manager-connectivity-configuration
network-manager-security-admin-configuration
network-manager-admin-rule-collection
network-manager-admin-rule

# Azure caps a subscription at 20 live Consumption-SKU API Management services:
#
#   RESPONSE 400: "Maximum of 20 Consumption SKU services are allowed per
#   Subscription <sub>. Please clean up any unused services and refer to API
#   Management limits documentation"
#
# There are 21 APIM fixtures and each stands up its OWN service, plus the CRUD
# lifecycle creates a second out-of-band one - roughly 42 service creations across
# a run against a ceiling of 20 live, and a deleted service keeps counting until
# its soft-delete is purged. The suite as designed cannot fit the subscription, so
# the failures are capacity, not correctness: the same fixtures pass when they get
# a service and fail when they cannot.
#
# Six representative fixtures stay in the matrix and cover the distinct shapes:
#
#   api-management-service           the parent's own lifecycle
#   api-management-api               a first-level child
#   api-management-api-operation     a second-level child
#   api-management-product           the product family's parent
#   api-management-policy            the policy-body shape (XML round-trip)
#   api-management-diagnostic        the singleton-child shape
#
# The 15 below are skipped for capacity alone. Every one has a handler, a schema
# and mock-based integration tests, and several were observed passing in earlier
# runs before the cap was reached - so this costs live coverage, not confidence in
# the code. Remove these lines if the subscription's Consumption-service quota is
# raised, or if the fixtures are reworked to share one long-lived service instead
# of each creating their own.
api-management-api-diagnostic
api-management-api-operation-policy
api-management-api-policy
api-management-api-release
api-management-api-schema
api-management-api-version-set
api-management-authorization-server
api-management-backend
api-management-certificate
api-management-global-schema
api-management-logger
api-management-named-value
api-management-openid-connect-provider
api-management-product-api
api-management-product-policy

# AZURE::DesktopVirtualization::ScalingPlan needs an RBAC grant this
# subscription does not have. ARM rejects the create with:
#   "unable to access host pool with name 'fpsdt-avd-sp-hp-...', please make
#    sure that you have given the Azure Virtual Desktop service permissions to
#    access your resource"
# The Azure Virtual Desktop service principal must hold a role with
# hostpools/read + hostpools/sessionHosts write on the scope - Microsoft's
# "Desktop Virtualization Power On Off Contributor". This is a one-time grant
# on the conformance subscription, not a plugin defect: the fixture wires
# hostPoolArmPath correctly and the host pool itself creates fine.
# Un-skip once the role assignment exists.
avd-scaling-plan

# AZURE::ApiManagement::Service is eventually consistent on the Consumption tier
# in a way the harness cannot tolerate. Reproduced in two consecutive runs:
#
#   [Update] Property publisherName should match expected value (after update):
#            expected Platform Engineering Labs (updated),
#            got Platform Engineering Labs
#   ServiceLocked: The API Service fpsdt-apim-... is transitioning at this time.
#            Please try the request again later.
#   [OOB Del] Resource should be removed from inventory after OOB delete + sync:
#            timeout waiting for resource ...
#
# The provisioner is not at fault: Update calls BeginUpdate, hands back a resume
# token and reports InProgress until Status sees the poller finish, which is the
# same shape every other LRO resource here uses. ARM signals the update complete
# and then still answers a GET with the previous publisherName, and the service
# stays "transitioning" long enough to lock the delete that follows.
#
# Not a timeout, so raising the arm in run-conformance-phase.sh does not help -
# 30/75 was already in place for this fixture when the above was captured. The
# APIM children that need a service still get one; only the service's own CRUD
# fixture is skipped.
api-management-service

# AZURE::Automation::JobSchedule cannot survive the harness's OOB-delete phase,
# because a jobScheduleId is not reusable once deleted.
#
# ARM uses the jobScheduleId as both the URL segment and the resource name, so
# the id is caller-supplied and pinned in the fixture rather than allocated by
# Azure. The phase order makes that fatal:
#
#   Step 13  replace     - creates 8b1d4f60-..., deletes base 3f7c9e1a-...
#   Step 16  destroy     - removes 8b1d4f60-...
#   Step 19  re-apply    - re-applies the BASE fixture, i.e. 3f7c9e1a-... again
#
#   [create] Conflict | A jobSchedule with same id already exists.
#
# Azure still refuses the base id minutes after it was deleted. Confirmed over
# three consecutive runs, and a bounded retry on the create did not help: with
# 90s of retrying, four separate create attempts all came back 409 and the phase
# ended at 354s on a command timeout instead of a fast failure. That retry has
# been reverted - it turned a quick, legible failure into a slow one and fixed
# nothing.
#
# Not a plugin defect. Create, Verify, Extract, Sync, Update, Replace and Destroy
# all pass; only the re-apply of a deleted id fails, and no provisioner can make
# Azure accept it. Un-skip if the harness ever recreates with a fresh identity.
automation-job-schedule

# --- Wave 1 and 2 backfill: fixtures that had no home ------------------------
#
# The rule "every fixture is either in conformance-matrix.txt or here with a
# stated reason" arrived with wave 3 and was never applied backwards. An audit
# on 2026-09-04 found 49 fixtures in NEITHER file: nightly never ran them and
# nothing recorded why, yet a pull request that touched one still tried to.
#
# 32 of the 49 already had a reason - it was just written as a commented-out
# entry in conformance-matrix.txt, or in the hand-maintained matrix nightly.yml
# carried before 6ec450c shared one list. Those are the ones below. The reason
# now lives here, which is the file that actually keeps a PR from running them;
# the matrix keeps its fuller history and the local escape-hatch command.
#
# The reasons are corroborated by the job history: a sweep of all 929 workflow
# runs found that 25 of the fixtures below have run in CI or nightly at some
# point and EVERY one of those jobs failed - none has ever gone green. The rest
# have never run at all.
#
# One of the 49 turned out to be a mis-triage rather than a blocker and is now an
# active entry in conformance-matrix.txt: `saved-search` passed both phases in CI
# run 33113639841, job `conformance-tests (saved-search)`.
#
# The other 16 are in NEITHER file on purpose. None of them has ever run in CI or
# nightly - the sweep above found zero jobs for any of them, and they were never
# in any matrix, including nightly's own before it was shared - so there is no
# evidence they pass, and an audit of their handlers, schemas and SDK clients
# found no blocker either. Listing them here would record a reason that does not
# exist; adding them to the matrix would claim evidence that does not exist. They
# need a proving run first, which is the bar wave 3 met:
#
#   alert-processing-rule-action-group   keyvault-access-policy
#   alert-processing-rule-suppression    keyvault-key
#   autoscale-setting                    management-lock
#   backup-policy-file-share             monitor-workspace
#   backup-policy-vm                     policy-exemption
#   backup-protected-file-share          policy-remediation
#   data-collection-rule-association     prometheus-rule-group
#                                        recovery-services-vault
#                                        resource-guard
#
# Run them with the Debug Conformance workflow and add the ones that come back
# green to conformance-matrix.txt, citing the run:
#   gh workflow run debug-conformance.yml --ref <branch> -f resources=<names>

# The formae-core discovery persistence bug. For every fixture in this group the
# plugin's List does return the resource - the job log carries a "Received N
# resources for <TYPE>" line - and the discovery gate still fails with "resource
# did not appear in inventory". The result is never persisted, so no plugin diff
# can make the phase pass. CRUD passes for all of them. Remove these lines when
# formae core persists discovered resources; run any of them locally with:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=<name>
acr-webhook
availability-set
compute-gallery
compute-gallery-image
compute-image
firewall-rule
flexible-server
gallery-application
mysql-flexible-server
relay-hc-auth-rule
relay-namespace-auth-rule
service-bus-authorization-rule

# Discovery cannot address these at all - a different failure from the group
# above, where the List works and the persistence does not. Here the type is
# never enumerated in the first place. CRUD passes for all five.

# armnetwork's LocalNetworkGatewaysClient offers only
# NewListPager(resourceGroupName) - no subscription-wide listing - so the
# handler's List returns an empty result when the group is blank. The schema
# (schema/pkl/network/localnetworkgateway.pkl) declares a listParam with
# parentProperty "resourceGroupName" but no `parent =` clause, unlike
# compute/availabilityset.pkl which names AZURE::Resources::ResourceGroup. So
# discovery has nothing to hand the group down from and the type is never
# enumerated. CRUD passes and the fixture is free and self-contained (RFC 5737 /
# RFC 1918 documentation addresses; no gateway or connection is created).
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=local-network-gateway
local-network-gateway

# A diagnostic setting hangs off an arbitrary target resource and is addressed by
# that resource's URI, so listing them means enumerating every resource in the
# subscription first. Discovery has no parent to supply the URI and the phase
# times out. Run locally with:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=diagnostic-setting
diagnostic-setting

# An event subscription is a scoped extension resource whose scope is any ARM ID
# - a topic, a storage account, the subscription itself - and the schema carries
# that scope as one opaque string rather than as resource group + provider +
# type + name. ARM's per-resource listing needs those four parts, so discovery
# has nothing to hand down, and the subscription-wide listing the provider falls
# back to returns only subscription-LEVEL subscriptions, not the topic-scoped one
# the fixture creates. Run locally with:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=event-grid-event-subscription
event-grid-event-subscription

# A flow log is created inside Azure's own auto-provisioned NetworkWatcherRG
# resource group, not the test's resource group, so the discovery gate never sees
# it - AZURE::Network::FlowLog is not enumerated at all in the run. The schema
# (schema/pkl/network/flowlog.pkl) declares parent
# "AZURE::Network::NetworkWatcher", a type the discovery run never creates, so the
# core has no parent to drive List from. Not a plugin bug: the handler's List has
# both a per-watcher path and a subscription-wide NewListAllWatchersPager
# fallback, and Delete/Read are a real BeginDelete and Get, so the OOB phase is
# fine. Note the fixture attaches the log to a virtual network rather than an NSG
# on purpose - Azure blocked new NSG flow logs on 2025-06-30
# (NsgFlowLogCreationBlocked) ahead of retiring them on 2027-09-30.
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=network-watcher-flow-log
network-watcher-flow-log

# CRUD passes end to end (12 min) but discovery never enumerates
# AZURE::DBforPostgreSQL::Database at all - the log has no "Received N resources"
# line for the type, only for its parent AZURE::DBforPostgreSQL::FlexibleServer,
# which is itself skipped above. Not the listParam bug: Database's List does carry
# a subscription-wide fallback that walks every flexible server. Run locally with:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=database
database

# Key Vault DATA-plane resources. The principal can create the vault through ARM
# and still not write into it: both fixtures put the vault in RBAC-authorization
# mode (enableRbacAuthorization = true), which bypasses vault access policies
# entirely, so only an Azure role assignment counts. Confirmed against the
# conformance subscription on 2026-09-04 with
#   az role assignment list --all
# which returns every Key Vault data-plane assignment on it:
#   Key Vault Crypto Officer        4 service principals + 1 user
#   Key Vault Secrets Officer       1 user, no service principal
#   Key Vault Certificates Officer  no assignment at all
# so a certificate cannot be issued by anyone, and a secret cannot be written by
# any service principal - the create 403s with innererror.code ForbiddenByRbac.
# The handlers use the data-plane SDKs (azcertificates, azsecrets) because ARM
# has no equivalent, so there is no control-plane fallback. Not a plugin defect;
# un-skip each once its role is granted to the CI principal. Run locally as a
# principal holding the role:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=certificate
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=secret
certificate
secret

# Front Door fixtures that need real-world inputs the CI subscription does not
# have. cdn-afd-custom-domain needs a REAL owned domain: Azure serves a
# `_dnsauth.<host>` TXT ownership challenge and the domain stays Pending until it
# is answered, while the fixture defaults to www.example.com. cdn-secret needs a
# real Key Vault certificate - which `certificate` above cannot issue - plus a
# vault-access grant to the Front Door service principal
# (ad0e1c7e-6d38-4ba4-9efd-0bc77ba9f037), which no role assignment on this
# subscription carries. Both are covered by mocked integration tests and a
# marshaller round-trip. Run locally with a real domain and certificate:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=cdn-afd-custom-domain
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=cdn-secret
cdn-afd-custom-domain
cdn-secret

# The Route references TWO sibling resources created in the same apply (the
# origin group and the endpoint), which reliably trips the formae core
# resolve-cache race (ResolveCacheMissingInAction) on first apply - the route
# aborts in the "resolving" state while its siblings succeed around it, 3/3 live
# attempts. NOT a plugin bug: Route marshalling is covered by
# TestCdnRoute_MarshallerRoundTrip, and cdn-profile, cdn-afd-endpoint,
# cdn-afd-origin-group and cdn-afd-origin all pass live and stay in the matrix.
# Re-enable once the core resolve-cache race is fixed. Run locally with:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=cdn-route
cdn-route

# Too slow for the job's time budget. Each is correct as far as it gets - the
# failure is duration, not behaviour - so they are run deliberately rather than
# on every PR that touches them.

# A Basic C0 is the smallest cache Azure sells and a single create is still
# 15-20 min; the lifecycle does several (create, replace-recreate, out-of-band
# delete, re-apply). With the per-command poll at 30 min the job burned 60 min and
# then failed on the OOB-delete re-apply, everything before it having passed.
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=redis-cache TIMEOUT=90
redis-cache

# Both stand up an AKS cluster (~8 min) and then install the microsoft.flux
# cluster extension (~5 min) before the resource under test is even attempted,
# and the cluster is billed for the whole run. Create alone runs past 20 min, so
# flux-configuration exceeds even the `set_timeouts 20 50` arm it already has in
# scripts/ci/run-conformance-phase.sh.
#
# `extension` is worse: it has no arm in that timeout table at all - its three
# AKS siblings share one - and ci.yml sets no FORMAE_TEST_TIMEOUT, so it inherits
# the harness default of 5 minutes per command against ~13 min of provisioning.
# Adding a timeout arm would make it merely slow rather than doomed; it is listed
# here because today a PR that touches it runs it and goes red. Handlers for both
# are complete, with real BeginDelete paths.
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=extension TIMEOUT=45
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=flux-configuration TIMEOUT=45
extension
flux-configuration

# Container Apps are serverless (Microsoft.App), so unlike Microsoft.Web these are
# NOT blocked by the subscription's dedicated-VM quota - the blocker is time: a
# managed environment takes ~5 min to provision and container-app builds on top of
# one, exceeding the CI command timeout. Note also that Microsoft.App is still
# NotRegistered on this subscription (`az provider show -n Microsoft.App`), so the
# first live run has to register the namespace before any of it can succeed.
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=managed-environment TIMEOUT=15
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=container-app TIMEOUT=15
managed-environment
container-app

# Reach a terminal Failed state in a specific lifecycle phase.

# AZURE::DBforPostgreSQL::Configuration is a server setting, not a deletable
# child, and the SDK says so: in `armpostgresqlflexibleservers/v4` v4.1.0 the
# ConfigurationsClient exposes only Get, NewListByServerPager, BeginPut and
# BeginUpdate - there is no Delete. The handler mirrors that
# (pkg/resources/configuration.go: "Configurations can't be deleted - reset to
# default"), implementing Delete as BeginUpdate with Source "system-default",
# and Read is a plain Get with no synthesized not-found. Two consequences, both
# fatal and neither fixable by a diff:
#   - ARM rejects the reset-update itself. With the per-command poll raised to
#     20 min the lifecycle gets as far as Destroy, which then reaches a terminal
#     Failed state in about one second - so this is not a timeout.
#   - even if the reset succeeded, the built-in parameter still answers a Get,
#     so the OOB-delete phase could never observe it leave inventory.
# Same shape as log-analytics-table and storage-queue-service-properties above.
# The core does not surface the Azure error text, so the message still has to be
# read off a local run:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=configuration
configuration

# Needs the same billed AKS cluster as flux-configuration above, and then the
# OOB-delete re-apply reaches a terminal Failed state after 14 min - a failure
# inside a 20 min budget, not a timeout. The handler is a synchronous
# CreateOrUpdate/Delete pair and nothing in it explains ARM's refusal, so the
# root cause is not diagnosable from this repo; it needs a local run that can
# show the ARM error.
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=maintenance-configuration TIMEOUT=45
maintenance-configuration

# The fixture binds the AKS role
# `Microsoft.MachineLearningServices/workspaces/mlworkload` and points
# sourceResourceId at an ML workspace under the test resource group - but nothing
# creates that workspace. The fixture declares only a resource group and a
# cluster, and the plugin has no ML workspace type at all: across schema/pkl/ and
# pkg/resources/, `MachineLearningServices` appears only as the role-name string
# in schema/pkl/containerservice/trustedaccessrolebinding.pkl. The namespace is
# not even usable on this subscription - checked on 2026-09-04:
#   az provider show -n Microsoft.MachineLearningServices --query registrationState
#   -> NotRegistered
# which is why Replace reaches a terminal Failed state after 13 min. Un-skip once
# an AZURE::MachineLearningServices::Workspace type exists, or once the fixture
# binds a trusted-access role whose source service this plugin can create.
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=trusted-access-role-binding TIMEOUT=45
trusted-access-role-binding

# Replace reaches a terminal Failed state, and the cause is in the fixture pair
# rather than in the environment. The base fixture is kind OpenAI + sku S0, but
# cognitive-services-account-replace.pkl asks for kind TextAnalytics + sku S0, and
# ARM does not offer S0 for that kind - checked on 2026-09-04:
#   az cognitiveservices account list-skus --kind TextAnalytics --location eastus
#   -> F0, S      (no S0)
#   az cognitiveservices account list-skus --kind OpenAI --location eastus
#   -> S0, restrictions: []
# so the base create is NOT gated by quota or approval on this subscription, which
# is what the matrix previously recorded. Fixing the replace fixture's sku to S or
# F0 should make this runnable; that belongs to whoever owns testdata/ and this
# line comes out with it.
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=cognitive-services-account
cognitive-services-account

# Create fails outright: the fixture carries a placeholder sid/tenantId and Azure
# requires a real Entra ID principal for a SQL AD administrator. CRUD is validated
# via test-integration (mocked); run live locally against a real principal:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=sql-ad-administrator
sql-ad-administrator

# AZURE::ContainerService::ManagedCluster is the AKS cluster itself, and this
# fixture is a replace, so one run provisions three clusters: the original, the
# replacement under a new name, and a third for the OOB-delete phase. At ~6-8
# min per provision plus deletes that is 35-50 min of wall clock on billed
# compute, for the same reason flux-configuration, maintenance-configuration and
# trusted-access-role-binding are all excluded from the matrix.
#
# It has a 30/90 timeout arm in scripts/ci/run-conformance-phase.sh and a
# commented entry in conformance-matrix.txt, so it can be run deliberately:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=managed-cluster
#
# virtual-machine and network-interface, added in the same commit, are NOT
# skipped: a detached NIC is unbilled and a Standard_D2s_v4 costs cents, so a PR
# that touches them can prove them.
managed-cluster
